title: Influence of special hand therapy rehabilitation on the subjective and functional outcome after surgically treated distal radius fracture
summary:
If you have broken a bone in your wrist (radius) in an accident, it may be necessary to operate on it.
If there are still problems in the injured wrist (e.g. when gripping or carrying), special hand therapy rehabilitation can be prescribed to improve hand function and pain so that you can get along well in everyday life again.
The aim of this study is to find out how this specific rehabilitation affects hand function, pain and personal well-being.
The test subject receives an information interview and, after an appropriate period of reflection, can consent to take part in the study.
First, a medical examination is carried out during which the range of motion and circumference of the hand is measured. Questions are then asked about pain, everyday activity and personal well-being. To do this, you will need to fill out three questionnaires, which will take approximately 15 minutes of your time. In addition, a hand strength measurement is carried out using a hand strength measuring device. The test subject then completes the therapy program for the prescribed period. At the end of the rehabilitation, there will be another medical examination, hand strength measurement, questions about pain, everyday activity and personal well-being. To do this, the three questionnaires must be filled out again.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Distal radius fracture
•	Unilateral injury
•	Ages 18-65 years 
•	Examination time from admission to hand rehabilitation
•	Surgical care
•	Receiving hand therapy rehabilitation
•	written declaration of consent regarding data collection
Exclusion criteria:
• Bilateral injury
• Additional bony injuries on the affected side
• Conservative care
